title: Godot agent alignment/linting tool to reduce token usage and inconsistencies
author: TheGAFF
selftext:
I have a rather large Godot game I've been working on for months now as a hobby, mostly using LLMs to do the work, and I've noticed that the code over time can get inconsistent in its naming, styling, and organization, even with gdstyle linting in place. Moreover, MD docs tend to get stale, scattered, huge, and easy for agents to miss, causing agents to have incorrect assumptions, wasting tokens, and just doing things you don't want it to do, resulting in having to give it yet another prompt before it gets it right.

Consequently, I've been building a tool alongside my game to help keep the code opinionated, organized, and consistent. It basically encourages your agent to self-correct and self-document the code it generates through linting rule errors. It's built on top of gdstyle, which is a popular linting tool in many existing Godot projects.

**Repo link**: https://github.com/TheGAFF/llm-lint-godot (there is a before/after table in the README to give you an idea of what to expect your code to be transformed into)

Have your agent install it and perhaps update your AGENTS.md to run the tool when its done with its work. (or use a skill/post-hook or whatever is trendy these days)

Overall features:

**Code de-duplication** - Uses heuristics (similar to a feature in JetBrain's IDEs) to detect duplicate code and encourages your agent to use a shared class. There are various thresholds of what is considered duplicate code because in many scenarios "duplicate code" is perfectly reasonable and expected.

*Role-based file names/functions* - keeps file/function names consistent, in appropriate folders, encouraging agents to keep like-features in one place, reducing token usage in many cases plus giving your agent the full picture of what a feature entails.

**Role-based self-healing docs** - this feature is a little experimental, but basically MD files have roles (ex. specification, guides, decisions) that require a review date to prevent staleness, have max document sizes, and enforced consistency. This keeps your MD files fresh, consistent, and concise.

Any feedback appreciated. I have similar tools in Typescript land (which is where most of my time is spent) but didn't see anything similar in Godot, so thought I'd give something to the Godot community since it is a great engine to work with.
